git-trim automatically trims local tracking branches whose upstream branches are merged or removed.

Installation

- Download a prebuilt binary from the Releases page and place it in a directory on your PATH.

GIT-TRIM(1)                                    General Commands Manual                                    GIT-TRIM(1)

NAME
       git-trim - Automatically trims your tracking branches whose upstream branches are merged or stray.

SYNOPSIS
       git-trim [FLAGS] [OPTIONS]

FLAGS
       -h, --help
              Prints help information

       --no-update
              Do not update remotes [config: trim.update]

       --no-confirm
              Do not ask confirm [config: trim.confirm]

       --no-detach
              Do not detach when HEAD is about to be deleted [config: trim.detach]

       --dry-run
              Do not delete branches, show what branches will be deleted

OPTIONS
       -b, --bases=bases
              Comma separated multiple names of branches. All the other branches are compared with the upstream
              branches of those branches. [default: branches that tracks `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/*/HEAD`]
              [config: trim.bases]

              The default value is a branch that tracks `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/*/HEAD`. They might not be
              reflected correctly when the HEAD branch of your remote repository is changed. You can see the changed
              HEAD branch name with `git remote show <remote>` and apply it to your local repository with `git remote
              set-head <remote> --auto`.

       -p, --protected=protected
              Comma separated multiple glob patterns (e.g. `release-*`, `feature/*`) of branches that should never be
              deleted. [config: trim.protected]

       --update-interval=update_interval
              Prevents too frequent updates. Seconds between updates in seconds. 0 to disable. [default: 5] [config:
              trim.updateInterval]

       -d, --delete=delete
              Comma separated values of `<delete range>[:<remote name>]`. Delete range is one of the `merged,
              merged-local, merged-remote, stray, diverged, local, remote`. `:<remote name>` is only necessary to a
              `<delete range>` when the range is applied to remote branches. You can use `*` as `<remote name>` to
              delete a range of branches from all remotes. [default : `merged:origin`] [config: trim.delete]

              `merged` implies `merged-local,merged-remote`.

              `merged-local` will delete merged tracking local branches. `merged-remote:<remote>` will delete merged
              upstream branches from `<remote>`. `stray` will delete tracking local branches, which is not merged,
              but the upstream is gone. `diverged:<remote>` will delete merged tracking local branches, and their
              upstreams from `<remote>` even if the upstreams are not merged and diverged from local ones. `local`
              will delete non-tracking merged local branches. `remote:<remote>` will delete non-upstream merged
              remote tracking branches. Use with caution when you are using other than `merged`. It might lose
              changes, and even nuke repositories.

EXIT STATUS
       0      Successful program execution.

       1      Unsuccessful program execution.

       101    The program panicked.

actions.command:
cat <<'SH' > /tmp/mk4.sh
set -e
R=/tmp/rr4; L=/tmp/lr4
rm -rf $R $L
git init -q --bare $R
git init -q -b master $L
cd $L
git config user.email a@b.c; git config user.name a
git remote add origin $R
echo m > master.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m c0
git push -q origin master:master
for b in b1 b2 b3; do
  git checkout -q -b $b master
  echo $b > $b.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m c$b
  git push -q origin $b:$b
done
git checkout -q master
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/master master
git remote set-head origin --auto
rm -f /tmp/shim/log.txt
PATH=/tmp/shim:$PATH /workspace/executable --dry-run 2>&1
echo "--- LOG ---"; cat /tmp/shim/log.txt
echo "--- synthetic commits in odb"
for o in $(ls .git/objects | grep -v pack); do for f in .git/objects/$o/*; do oid="$o$(basename $f)"; if git cat-file -p $oid 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'git-trim: squash merge test'; then echo "$oid"; fi; done; done
SH
bash /tmp/mk4.sh

Hmm interesting. So order: for each branch (local first, then upstream): direct ref, then synthetic.

Wait: order was develop, synthetic_local, origin/develop, synthetic_upstream. Hmm, but in lr2 (where local == upstream oid), the calls were: develop, synthetic, origin/develop, synthetic. Earlier in lr2 I only found one synthetic commit `20e0a419` and both calls used it. So in lr2, only one synthetic commit was created because... the tree was identical? Hmm, unless in lr2, the tool only created one synthetic commit because... hmm. Wait in lr2 I ran `mk2.sh` then set-head etc. and ran the executable ONCE. So two synthetic commits should exist. Let me recheck lr2's object DB.

Actually hold on, in lr2, maybe the second call reused the cached synthetic because the tree was the same? No — timestamps differ so OIDs differ.

- `[base]` for base branches

- `[merged, but: HEAD]`

Are there other annotations? Let's explore. Maybe `[merged, but: PROTECTED]` for protected branches? Let's test with `-p`.

- `merged` = merged-local + merged-remote
- `merged-local`
- `merged-remote:<remote>`
- `stray`
- `diverged:<remote>`
- `local`
- `remote:<remote>`

Let me test each. But first, let's understand the branch model:

Local branch states:
- tracking (has upstream): branch.X.remote config set + refs/remotes/<remote>/<name> exists
- non-tracking: no upstream

Remote refs: refs/remotes/<remote>/<name>

Categories:
- `merged-local`: tracking local branch that is merged into base
- `merged-remote`: remote ref that is the upstream of some tracking local branch and is merged into base
- `stray`: tracking local branch that is NOT merged but its upstream is gone
- `diverged:<remote>`: "delete merged tracking local branches, and their upstreams from <remote> even if the upstreams are not merged and diverged from local ones"

Hmm, "diverged" — delete the local merged branch AND its upstream even if upstream is not merged/diverged.
- `local`: non-tracking merged local branches
- `remote:<remote>`: non-upstream merged remote tracking branches

Let me test each systematically. But first, let me understand what determines "merged". 

`git branch --format %(refname) --merged refs/remotes/origin/master` gives local branches merged into base.
`git branch --format %(refname) --remote --merged refs/remotes/origin/master` gives remote refs merged into base.

Then for each non-merged branch, the squash test is applied (via synthetic commits).

"git-trim automatically trims your tracking branches whose upstream branches are merged or stray."

So the core idea: a local branch L tracking upstream U. If U is merged into base, then L's content is in base → L can be deleted. If U is gone (removed from remote), then L is "stray" → deleted? No — `stray` is a separate delete range.

Hmm, "whose upstream branches are merged or stray" — so: L tracks U. If U is merged into base (i.e., U's changes are in the base), then L can be deleted (merged-local). And if U is deleted from the remote (stray), then L is stray.

Hmm, but actually, wait. Is the synthetic commit created per (branch, base) pair or per branch? The parent is fixed per invocation. Let me test with 2 bases.

Let me also think about whether the synthetic test is applied when the branch is an ancestor of the base — no, `git branch --merged` handles that, and the direct rev-list test returns empty for ancestors anyway... Actually hold on: `git branch --merged <ref>` gives ancestry. And the rev-list direct test: for an ancestor X of base, `base...X` has no right-side commits → empty → merged. So consistent.

Hmm, but actually since `git branch --merged base` is computed first (giving the merged set), and the rev-list tests are only run for branches NOT in that set... But then the direct rev-list test would be redundant... unless it's needed for a different purpose.

Hmm! Wait. Maybe the rev-list tests are for a *different* purpose: determining whether the local branch and its upstream are "in sync". Let me reconsider.

Hmm, alternatively:

Now the synthetic test catches the squash case.

OK. But hmm, there's a subtlety: the synthetic commit's parent is the base, so its diff = base_tree → X_tree. That's the "total" difference. For a squash-merged branch, base contains a commit with that exact patch-id. ✓

Now, one important question: does the tool run these tests for the *local* branch and the *upstream* branch separately, with the same base? Yes it appears so.

Hmm, but hold on: would you delete U if L is not merged? That seems dangerous but that's what the doc says. Let me test.

Also `stray`: tracking local branch that is not merged but its upstream is gone. Let me test that.

Let me build a comprehensive scenario with all these cases. But first, let me understand more precisely the base branch detection and the "pair" concept.

Let me now test `stray`.

Scenario lr15:

- local: master (tracks origin/master), develop (tracks origin/develop)
- delete origin/develop from remote (so develop's upstream is gone)
- develop has unmerged work
Then: develop is "stray" → with `--delete stray` it should be deleted.

Let's test.

So with no `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, it fails BEFORE any git command. So the base detection uses libgit2 to look up `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`. Hmm, but how does it know the remote name? From config `remote.origin.url`.

Hmm, actually: maybe it iterates over config entries `remote.*.url`, and for each remote, looks up the ref `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD` via git2's ref lookup. If the ref doesn't resolve → no base.

Hmm, but hold on: after `git remote update --prune` (which fetches), the `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`... hmm, `git fetch --prune` doesn't create origin/HEAD. Actually `git remote update` does create `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`? Hmm, no. Actually `git fetch` sets up `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD` only via `git remote set-head`. Hmm, but actually `git fetch origin` in newer git versions does create `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` automatically? Let me check: git's `builtin/fetch.c` has `find_unique_abbrev_oid`... Actually, `git fetch` with `--prune`? Hmm.

In my tests, `git remote update --prune` did NOT create refs/remotes/origin/HEAD (in mk11 the file list showed refs/remotes/origin/HEAD created by set-head). Hmm.

Wait, but actually there's this in git: when fetching, if `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD` doesn't exist, git may create it. Actually I recall git 2.x: `git fetch` calls `set_head` if... Hmm. There's `git fetch --set-upstream`? No.

Hmm, actually I recall `git ls-remote` and `git fetch` negotiating `symref` capability.

Let's test empirically.

<oid>	HEAD
...

Actually, here's a thought: maybe it does:

Hmm. Let's think about why ls-remote is called at all. Let's test: what if the remote's HEAD differs from the local refs/remotes/origin/HEAD?

Let me test that: set refs/remotes/origin/HEAD → master, but the remote's actual HEAD is develop.

static int loose_backend__writestream_finalize(git_odb_stream *_stream, const git_oid *oid)
{
	loose_writestream *stream = (loose_writestream *)_stream;
	loose_backend *backend = (loose_backend *)_stream->backend;
	git_str final_path = GIT_STR_INIT;
	int error = 0;

	if (object_file_name(&final_path, backend, oid) < 0 ||
		object_mkdir(&final_path, backend) < 0)
		error = -1;
	else
		error = git_filebuf_commit_at(

	git_str_dispose(&final_path);

	return error;
}

	loose_writestream *stream = (loose_writestream *)_stream;

static int filebuf_flags(loose_backend *backend)
{
	int flags = GIT_FILEBUF_TEMPORARY |

}

static int hash_header(git_hash_ctx *ctx, git_object_size_t size, git_object_t type)
{
	char header[64];
	size_t hdrlen;
	int error;

	 if ((error = git_odb__format_object_header(&hdrlen,
		header, sizeof(header), size, type)) < 0)
		return error;

	return git_hash_update(ctx, header, hdrlen);
}

int git_odb_open_wstream(
	git_odb_stream **stream, git_odb *db, git_object_size_t size, git_object_t type)
{
	size_t i, writes = 0;
	int error = GIT_ERROR;
	git_hash_ctx *ctx = NULL;

	GIT_ASSERT_ARG(stream);
	GIT_ASSERT_ARG(db);

	if ((error = git_mutex_lock(&db->lock)) < 0) {
		git_error_set(GIT_ERROR_ODB, "failed to acquire the odb lock");
		return error;
	}
	error = GIT_ERROR;
	for (i = 0; i < db->backends.length && error < 0; ++i) {
		backend_internal *internal = git_vector_get(&db->backends, i);
		git_odb_backend *b = internal->backend;

		/* we don't write in alternates! */
		if (internal->is_alternate)
			continue;

		if (b->writestream != NULL) {
			++writes;
			error = b->writestream(stream, b, size, type);
		} else if (b->write != NULL) {
			++writes;
			error = init_fake_wstream(stream, b, size, type);
		}
	}
	git_mutex_unlock(&db->lock);

	if (error < 0) {
		if (error == GIT_PASSTHROUGH)
			error = 0;
		else if (!writes)
			error = git_odb__error_unsupported_in_backend("write object");

		goto done;
	}

	ctx = git__malloc(sizeof(git_hash_ctx));
	GIT_ERROR_CHECK_ALLOC(ctx);

	if ((error = git_hash_ctx_init(ctx, git_oid_algorithm(db->options.oid_type))) < 0 ||
	    (error = hash_header(ctx, size, type)) < 0)
		goto done;

#ifdef GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256
	(*stream)->oid_type = db->options.oid_type;
#endif
	(*stream)->hash_ctx = ctx;
	(*stream)->declared_size = size;
	(*stream)->received_bytes = 0;

done:
	if (error)
		git__free(ctx);
	return error;
}

static int git_odb_stream__invalid_length(
	const git_odb_stream *stream,
	const char *action)
{
	git_error_set(GIT_ERROR_ODB,
		"cannot %s - "
		"Invalid length. %"PRId64" was expected. The "
		"total size of the received chunks amounts to %"PRId64".",
		action, stream->declared_size, stream->received_bytes);

	return -1;
}

int git_odb_stream_write(git_odb_stream *stream, const char *buffer, size_t len)
{
	git_hash_update(stream->hash_ctx, buffer, len);

	stream->received_bytes += len;

	if (stream->received_bytes > stream->declared_size)
		return git_odb_stream__invalid_length(stream,
			"stream_write()");

	return stream->write(stream, buffer, len);
}

int git_odb_stream_finalize_write(git_oid *out, git_odb_stream *stream)
{
	if (stream->received_bytes != stream->declared_size)
		return git_odb_stream__invalid_length(stream,
			"stream_finalize_write()");

	git_hash_final(out->id, stream->hash_ctx);

#ifdef GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256
	out->type = stream->oid_type;
#endif

	if (git_odb__freshen(stream->backend->odb, out))
		return 0;

static void current_time(time_t *now_out, int *offset_out)
{
	time_t offset;
	struct tm _utc, *utc_tm;

	/*
	 * Get the current time as seconds since the epoch and
	 * transform that into a tm struct containing the time at
	 * UTC. Give that to mktime which considers it a local time
	 * (tm_isdst = -1 asks it to take DST into account) and gives
	 * us that time as seconds since the epoch. The difference
	 * between its return value and 'now' is our offset to UTC.
	 */
	time(now_out);
	utc_tm = p_gmtime_r(now_out, &_utc);
	utc_tm->tm_isdst = -1;
	offset = (time_t)difftime(*now_out, mktime(utc_tm));
	offset /= 60;

	*offset_out = (int)offset;
}

cd $L
git config user.email a@b.c; git config user.name a
git remote add origin $R
echo m>master.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m c0
git push -q origin master
# pair: plain (both merged later)
git branch -q plain master
git push -q origin plain
# pair: unmerged
git checkout -q -b unmerged master; echo u>unmerged.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cu1
git push -q origin unmerged
# pair: div (L merged, U diverged)
git checkout -q -b div master; echo v>v.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cv1
git push -q origin div
# pair: up (U merged, L not merged)
git checkout -q -b up master; echo w>w.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cw1
git push -q origin up
# pair: stray
git checkout -q -b stray master; echo s>s.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cs1
git push -q origin stray
# advance master to include plain and div's v1 and up's w1
git checkout -q master
git merge -q --ff-only div
git merge -q --ff-only up
git commit -q --allow-empty -m c0b
git push -q origin master
# make div's upstream diverged
git checkout -q -b tempdiv origin/div; echo v2>v2.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cv2
git push -q origin tempdiv:div
git checkout -q master; git branch -q -D tempdiv
# local-only extra commit on up
git checkout -q up; echo w2>w2.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cw2
# remove stray from remote
git checkout -q master; git push -q origin --delete stray
# set tracking
git checkout -q master
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/master master
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/plain plain
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/unmerged unmerged
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/div div
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/up up
git remote set-head origin --auto
git branch -a -vv
SH
bash /tmp/mk22.sh && cd /tmp/lr22 && echo "=== default ==="; PATH=/tmp/shim:$PATH /workspace/executable --dry-run 2>/dev/null; echo "=== diverged:origin ==="; PATH=/tmp/shim:$PATH /workspace/executable --dry-run --delete diverged:origin 2>/dev/null; echo "=== merged:origin ==="; PATH=/tmp/shim:$PATH /workspace/executable --dry-run --delete merged:origin 2>/dev/null

actions.command:
cat <<'SH' > /tmp/mk22.sh
set -e
R=/tmp/rr22; L=/tmp/lr22
rm -rf $R $L
git init -q --bare $R
git init -q -b master $L
cd $L
git config user.email a@b.c; git config user.name a
git remote add origin $R
echo m>master.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m c0
git push -q origin master
git branch -q plain master; git push -q origin plain
git checkout -q -b unmerged master; echo u>unmerged.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cu1; git push -q origin unmerged
git checkout -q -b stray master; echo s>s.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cs1; git push -q origin stray
# up: L will have extra local commit
git checkout -q -b up master; echo w>w.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cw1; git push -q origin up
git checkout -q master; git merge -q --ff-only origin/up
# div
git checkout -q -b div master; echo v>v.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cv1; git push -q origin div
git checkout -q master; git merge -q --ff-only div
git commit -q --allow-empty -m c0b; git push -q origin master
# make origin/div diverged (extra commit on remote only)
git checkout -q -b tempdiv origin/div; echo v2>v2.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cv2; git push -q origin tempdiv:div
git checkout -q master; git branch -q -D tempdiv
# extra local commit on up
git checkout -q up; echo w2>w2.txt; git add -A; git commit -q -m cw2
git checkout -q master
# remove stray from remote
git push -q origin --delete stray
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/master master
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/plain plain
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/unmerged unmerged
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/div div
git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/up up
git remote set-head origin --auto
git branch -a -vv
SH
bash /tmp/mk22.sh && cd /tmp/lr22 && echo "=== default ==="; PATH=/tmp/shim:$PATH /workspace/executable --dry-run 2>/dev/null; echo "=== diverged:origin ==="; PATH=/tmp/shim:$PATH /workspace/executable --dry-run --delete diverged:origin 2>/dev/null

cat <<'SH' > /tmp/keys.sh
repo=$1; shift
(tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null
tmux new-session -d -s tt -x 220 -y 60 >/dev/null 2>&1
sleep 0.6
tmux send-keys -t tt "cd $repo && PATH=/tmp/shim:\$PATH /workspace/executable --no-update 1>/tmp/o.txt; echo EXIT=\$? > /tmp/exit.txt" Enter
sleep 3
for k in "$@"; do
  tmux send-keys -t tt "$k"
  sleep 1.5
done
sleep 2
echo "--- pane ---"
tmux capture-pane -t tt -p -S -300 | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' | tail -8
echo "--- exit ---"; cat /tmp/exit.txt 2>/dev/null
SH
echo "##### ESC"; bash /tmp/mk22.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; bash /tmp/keys.sh /tmp/lr22 Escape
echo "##### Ctrl+C"; bash /tmp/mk22.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; bash /tmp/keys.sh /tmp/lr22 C-c
echo "##### Ctrl+D"; bash /tmp/mk22.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; bash /tmp/keys.sh /tmp/lr22 C-d

    /// Writes argument's help to the wrapped stream.
    fn help(
        &mut self,
        arg: Option<&Arg>,
        about: &StyledStr,
        spec_vals: &str,
        next_line_help: bool,
        longest: usize,
    ) {
        debug!("HelpTemplate::help");
        use std::fmt::Write as _;
        let literal = &self.styles.get_literal();

        // Is help on next line, if so then indent
        if next_line_help {
            debug!("HelpTemplate::help: Next Line...{next_line_help:?}");
            self.writer.push_str("\n");
            self.writer.push_str(TAB);
            self.writer.push_str(NEXT_LINE_INDENT);
        }

        let spaces = if next_line_help {
            TAB.len() + NEXT_LINE_INDENT.len()
        } else {
            longest + TAB_WIDTH * 2
        };
        let trailing_indent = spaces; // Don't indent any further than the first line is indented
        let trailing_indent = self.get_spaces(trailing_indent);

        let mut help = about.clone();
        let mut help_is_empty = help.is_empty();
        help.replace_newline_var();

        let next_line_specs = self.use_long && arg.is_some();
        if !spec_vals.is_empty() && !next_line_specs {
            if !help_is_empty {
                let sep = " ";
                help.push_str(sep);
            }
            help.push_str(spec_vals);
            help_is_empty = help.is_empty();
        }

        let avail_chars = self.term_w.saturating_sub(spaces);
        debug!(
            "HelpTemplate::help: help_width={}, spaces={}, avail={}",
            spaces,
            help.display_width(),
            avail_chars
        );
        help.wrap(avail_chars);
        help.indent("", &trailing_indent);
        self.writer.push_styled(&help);

        let mut has_possible_values = false;
        if let Some(arg) = arg {
            if !arg.is_hide_possible_values_set() && self.use_long_pv(arg) {
                const DASH_SPACE: usize = "- ".len();
                let possible_vals = arg.get_possible_values();
                if !possible_vals.is_empty() {
                    debug!("HelpTemplate::help: Found possible vals...{possible_vals:?}");
                    has_possible_values = true;

                    let longest = possible_vals
                        .iter()
                        .filter(|f| !f.is_hide_set())
                        .map(|f| display_width(f.get_name()))
                        .max()
                        .expect("Only called with possible value");

                    let spaces = spaces + TAB_WIDTH - DASH_SPACE;

#!/bin/bash
echo "GIT: $*" >> /tmp/shim/log.txt
cmd="$*"
rules=/tmp/shim/rules.txt
if [ -f "$rules" ]; then
  while IFS='|' read -r pat mode; do
    [ -z "$pat" ] && continue
    case "$cmd" in
      *"$pat"*) ;;
      *) continue;;
    esac
    case "$mode" in
      stripheads) /usr/bin/git "$@" | sed 's|^refs/heads/||'; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]} ;;
      addlocalbogus) /usr/bin/git "$@" | sed '1i refs/heads/bogusbranch'; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]} ;;
    esac
  done < "$rules"
fi
exec /usr/bin/git "$@"
EOF

#!/bin/bash

cmd="$*"
rules=/tmp/shim/rules.txt

  while IFS='|' read -r pat mode; do
    [ -z "$pat" ] && continue
    case "$cmd" in
      *"$pat"*) ;;
      *) continue;;
    esac
    case "$mode" in

const char *git_commit_summary(git_commit *commit)
{
	git_str summary = GIT_STR_INIT;
	const char *msg, *space, *next;
	bool space_contains_newline = false;

	GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(commit, NULL);

	if (!commit->summary) {
		for (msg = git_commit_message(commit), space = NULL; *msg; ++msg) {
			char next_character = msg[0];
			/* stop processing at the end of the first paragraph */
			if (next_character == '\n') {
				if (!msg[1])
					break;
				if (msg[1] == '\n')
					break;
				/* stop processing if next line contains only whitespace */
				next = msg + 1;
				while (*next && git__isspace_nonlf(*next)) {
					++next;
				}
				if (!*next || *next == '\n')
					break;
			}
			/* record the beginning of contiguous whitespace runs */
			if (git__isspace(next_character)) {
				if(space == NULL) {
					space = msg;
					space_contains_newline = false;
				}
				space_contains_newline |= next_character == '\n';
			}
			/* the next character is non-space */
			else {
				/* process any recorded whitespace */
				if (space) {
					if(space_contains_newline)
						git_str_putc(&summary, ' '); /* if the space contains a newline, collapse to ' ' */
					else
						git_str_put(&summary, space, (msg - space)); /* otherwise copy it */
					space = NULL;
				}
				/* copy the next character */
				git_str_putc(&summary, next_character);
			}
		}

		commit->summary = git_str_detach(&summary);
		if (!commit->summary)
			commit->summary = git__strdup("");
	}

	return commit->summary;
}

    /// Run `git` and return its standard output, discarding its standard error.
    ///
    /// `git-trim` re-implements the reporting itself, so `git`'s own chatter would only confuse
    /// the output; the exit status is translated into an `io::Error` carrying the exit code.
    pub fn capture(&self, args: &[&str]) -> io::Result<String> {
        let _ = args;

        let mut cmd = self.command();
        cmd.stdin(Stdio::null());
        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());
        cmd.stderr(Stdio::null());
        let output = cmd.output()?;
        if !output.status.success() {
            let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);
            return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(code));
        }
        Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).into_owned())
    }

    /// Run `git` letting it write to our own stdout/stderr, and fail when it exits non-zero.
    pub fn run(&self, args: &[&str]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let status = self
            .command()
            .args(args)
            .status()
            .with_context(|| format!("failed to run `git {}`", args.join(" ")))?;
        if !status.success() {
            let code = status.code().unwrap_or(-1);
            return Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(code).into());
        }
        Ok(())
</output>

<output>
    refname: &str,
    merged: &mut HashMap<String, bool>,
    pending: &mut Vec<(String, usize)>,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    if merged.contains_key(refname) {
        return Ok(());
    }
    eprintln!("DBG4 enter refname={}", refname);
    let mut result = false;
    for (index, base) in bases.iter().enumerate() {
        if ancestry_contains(ancestry, &base.refname, refname) {
            result = true;
            break;
        }
        let output = match git.cherry_pick_right_only(&base.refname, refname) {
            Ok(output) => output,
            Err(err) => {
                eprintln!("DBG5 cherry error refname={} {}", refname, err);
                return Err(anyhow::Error::from(err));
            }
        };
        if crate::branch::cherry_pick_is_empty(&output) {
            result = true;
            break;
        }
        pending.push((refname.to_string(), index));
    eprintln!("DBG3 refname={} result={}", refname, result);
    }
    merged.insert(refname.to_string(), result);
    Ok(())
}

/// Names a branch is known by, in the order the protection check considers them.
</output>

    pub fn cherry_pick(&mut self, git: &Git, base: &str, refname: &str) -> anyhow::Result<bool> {
        let oid = self.commit_oid(refname)?;
        if self.cached(oid, base) == Some(true) {
            return Ok(true);
        }
        let output = git.cherry_pick_right_only(base, refname)?;
        let merged = cherry_pick_is_empty(&output);
        if merged {
            self.cache.insert((oid, base.to_string()), true);
        }
        Ok(merged)
    }

    /// Run the squash-merge probe for `refname` against `base` and memoise the result.
    pub fn probe_squash(
        &mut self,
        git: &Git,
        base: &str,
        refname: &str,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<bool> {
        let oid = self.commit_oid(refname)?;
        if let Some(true) = self.cached(oid, base) {
            return Ok(true);
        }
        let squash = self.squash_commit(base, refname)?;
        let output = git.cherry_pick_right_only(base, &format!("{}", squash))?;
        let merged = cherry_pick_is_empty(&output);
        if merged {
            self.cache.insert((oid, base.to_string()), true);
        }
        Ok(merged)
    }
}

{"command": "cd /workspace && cat <<'EOF' > compile.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds the `git-trim` executable into ./executable.
#
# Dependencies are resolved from the local cargo registry cache when there is no network; the
# Cargo.lock committed with the sources pins the exact versions that were used.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

if [ -z "${CARGO_HOME:-}" ] && [ -d /usr/local/cargo ]; then
    export CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo
fi

cargo build --release --offline

cp -f target/release/git-trim executable
chmod +x executable
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh
cat <<'EOF' > AGENT_REPORT.md
# git-trim reimplementation

`./executable` is a Rust rewrite of the `git-trim 0.4.4` command, reverse engineered purely from
observing the provided binary (its `--help`, its stdout/stderr, its exit codes and the `git`
commands it spawns, observed through a `git` shim placed earlier on `PATH`).

## Layout

* `Cargo.toml` - crate manifest; dependencies are `anyhow`, `clap` (builder API, no derive),
  `git2` (libgit2) and `libc`.
* `src/cli.rs` - clap command definition; `-h`/`--help`/`-V` outputs are byte-identical to the
  original (the `help`/`version` args are hidden, `next_line_help` is on, `wrap_help` is off).
* `src/config.rs` - `trim.*` configuration plus the `--delete` range grammar and its error strings.
* `src/glob.rs` - small glob matcher used for `--protected` (`*`, `?`, `[...]`, `\` escapes, no
  brace alternation).
* `src/gitproc.rs` - spawning `git -C <workdir> ...`; analysis commands capture their output,
  deletion commands inherit stdout/stderr.
* `src/branch.rs` - branch model, output parsers (with the `assert!`s the original panics with in
  `src/branch.rs`), remote HEAD parsing, worktree parsing and the squash-merge probe that writes
  the synthetic `git-trim: squash merge test` commit into the object database.
* `src/remote.rs` - remote listing (`git remote update --prune`), `git ls-remote --symref` HEADs.
* `src/scan.rs` - base branch resolution (`--bases`/`trim.bases`/`refs/remotes/*/HEAD`), the
  ancestry/cherry-pick/squash classification and the skip-reason computation.
* `src/report.rs` - "Branches that will remain" report, the `Delete ...` sections and the actual
  deletion (`git push --delete --no-verify [--dry-run]`, optional `git checkout <refname>` detach,
  `git branch --delete --force`).
* `src/prompt.rs` + `src/tty.rs` - the `Confirm? [y/N] ` dialoguer-compatible prompt (raw mode,
  ANSI hide/show cursor, `Cancelled` on decline) and terminal detection/raw mode helpers.
* `src/main.rs` - orchestration, error reporting via anyhow (`Error: ...\n\nCaused by:\n    ...`).

## Verified behaviour

Compared against the original on ~15 repositories and many flag combinations: classification of
merged / squash-merged / diverged / stray / unmerged tracking pairs, non-tracking and non-upstream
branches, `--delete` ranges (`merged`, `merged-local`, `merged-remote:<r>`, `stray`, `diverged:<r>`,
`local`, `remote:<r>`, `*`), `--protected` globs, `--bases` spellings, `--dry-run`, `--no-update`,
`--no-detach`, `--no-confirm`, worktrees, detached-HEAD advice text, multiple remotes and the
out-of-sync warning. The `git` subprocess log matches as well.

## Known differences / remaining work

* Deletion order inside a run is `HashSet`-driven in the original and therefore nondeterministic;
  this implementation sorts deterministically. Displayed lists that the original sorts are sorted
  here too, while the "Branches that will remain" listing follows the repository's reference order
  (loose refs before packed refs), exactly like the original.
* The synthetic squash-merge commit carries the current timestamp, so its oid always differs from
  the original's; the merge verdict is unaffected.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds the `git-trim` executable into ./executable.
#
# Dependencies are resolved from the local cargo registry cache when there is no network; the
# Cargo.lock committed with the sources pins the exact versions that were used.

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

if [ -z "${CARGO_HOME:-}" ] && [ -d /usr/local/cargo ]; then
    export CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo
fi

cargo build --release --offline

cp -f target/release/git-trim executable
chmod +x executable
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh
cat <<'EOF' > AGENT_REPORT.md
# git-trim reimplementation

`./executable` is a Rust rewrite of the `git-trim 0.4.4` command, reverse engineered purely from
observing the provided binary (its `--help`, its stdout/stderr, its exit codes and the `git`
commands it spawns, observed through a `git` shim placed earlier on `PATH`).

## Layout

* `Cargo.toml` - crate manifest; dependencies are `anyhow`, `clap` (builder API, no derive),
  `git2` (libgit2) and `libc`.
* `src/cli.rs` - clap command definition; `-h`/`--help`/`-V` outputs are byte-identical to the
  original (the `help`/`version` args are hidden, `next_line_help` is on, `wrap_help` is off).
* `src/config.rs` - `trim.*` configuration plus the `--delete` range grammar and its error strings.
* `src/glob.rs` - small glob matcher used for `--protected` (`*`, `?`, `[...]`, `\` escapes, no
  brace alternation).
* `src/gitproc.rs` - spawning `git -C <workdir> ...`; analysis commands capture their output,
  deletion commands inherit stdout/stderr.
* `src/branch.rs` - branch model, output parsers (with the `assert!`s the original panics with in
  `src/branch.rs`), remote HEAD parsing, worktree parsing and the squash-merge probe that writes
  the synthetic `git-trim: squash merge test` commit into the object database.
* `src/remote.rs` - remote listing (`git remote update --prune`), `git ls-remote --symref` HEADs.
* `src/scan.rs` - base branch resolution (`--bases`/`trim.bases`/`refs/remotes/*/HEAD`), the
  ancestry/cherry-pick/squash classification and the skip-reason computation.
* `src/report.rs` - "Branches that will remain" report, the `Delete ...` sections and the actual
  deletion (`git push --delete --no-verify [--dry-run]`, optional `git checkout <refname>` detach,
  `git branch --delete --force`).
* `src/prompt.rs` + `src/tty.rs` - the `Confirm? [y/N] ` dialoguer-compatible prompt (raw mode,
  ANSI hide/show cursor, `Cancelled` on decline) and terminal detection/raw mode helpers.
* `src/main.rs` - orchestration, error reporting via anyhow (`Error: ...\n\nCaused by:\n    ...`).

## Verified behaviour

Compared against the original on ~15 repositories and many flag combinations: classification of
merged / squash-merged / diverged / stray / unmerged tracking pairs, non-tracking and non-upstream
branches, `--delete` ranges (`merged`, `merged-local`, `merged-remote:<r>`, `stray`, `diverged:<r>`,
`local`, `remote:<r>`, `*`), `--protected` globs, `--bases` spellings, `--dry-run`, `--no-update`,
`--no-detach`, `--no-confirm`, worktrees, detached-HEAD advice text, multiple remotes and the
out-of-sync warning. The `git` subprocess log matches as well.

## Known differences / remaining work

* Deletion order inside a run is `HashSet`-driven in the original and therefore nondeterministic;
  this implementation sorts deterministically. Displayed lists that the original sorts are sorted
  here too, while the "Branches that will remain" listing follows the repository's reference order
  (loose refs before packed refs), exactly like the original.
* The synthetic squash-merge commit carries the current timestamp, so its oid always differs from
  the original's; the merge verdict is unaffected.
* Panics triggered by corrupting `git` output reproduce the same assertions and messages, but the
  `src/branch.rs` line numbers of the original (22 and 93) are not reproduced.
* `--update-interval` is parsed (clap i64 errors match) but has no observable effect in the
  original either, so it is validated and otherwise ignored.
* Behaviour with `trim.updateInterval` set in the *system* config and some exotic base spellings
  (`refs/notes/...`, tags) were only spot-checked.
EOF
